Targets: rv64 +v, rv32 +v, rv64 +zve32x, rv32 +zve64d,+zvl128b, rv64 +v,+zvl256b, rv32 +m, rv64 +m,+f,+d, rv32 (bare), rv32 +xcvsimd,+m, rv32 +m,+xpulpimg. Cost kinds throughput, latency, code-size, size-latency. Output is byte-identical in every valid combination. The only differing runs were invalid inputs (scalable IR on non-V targets, i64 elements on zve32x) that assert identically in both builds; only the stack-trace addresses and paths differ.

Xpulpv2 costs (rv32 +xpulpv,+zfinx, logs/20-F004.cost.ll re-run by me): load/store v2i16/v4i8 1, constant-vector store 4, add/sub/and/shl/smax/abs 1, mul v2i16 5 (ISD::MUL is Expand for these types, lowering :674, so it is scalarised), icmp 1, select 3 (VSELECT Expand), extract/insert 1, shuffles 1, sext 3, trunc 0, bitcast 1, reduce.add 3. Sensible for a first model. The integration-head build asserts (getMinRVVVectorSizeInBits) on the first v2i16 load.

Non-blocking observation: like upstream's P-extension guards, the hasPULPExtV2 guards cover ANY fixed vector (e.g. <16 x i8> shuffles and extracts cost 1, which underestimates them) and would also override RVV costs if Xpulpv2 and V were ever enabled together. This matches upstream's choice and its TODO, and V+Xpulpv2 is not a supported GAP9 configuration. A finer model is a follow-up, not a reason to reject.
